title: Magento Development Agency in Dallas
metaTitle: Magento Development Agency in Dallas, TX | TDM
metaDescription: Magento and Adobe Commerce for Dallas distributors and retailers: B2B pricing, ERP integration, performance tuning, upgrades and support.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) builds, extends and maintains Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce stores for Dallas companies, working remotely. Magento suits merchants whose needs go beyond a simple cart: large catalogues, customer-specific pricing, several storefronts and deep links to ERP or warehouse systems. Dallas is a distribution city, and that description fits a large number of the wholesalers, suppliers and multi-brand retailers based around it.

sections.heading: Why Magento has a place in North Texas
paragraphs: The region's road, rail and air links have filled it with distribution businesses. Industrial suppliers, building material merchants, auto parts wholesalers, foodservice distributors and medical supply companies operate from warehouses along the interstates and around the airport. Their customers are other businesses that expect to log in, see their negotiated prices, reorder from a past invoice and pay on account. That is ordinary work for Magento and hard work for lighter platforms.

Catalogue size is the other reason. A distributor may carry tens of thousands of SKUs with attributes such as dimensions, fitment or material grade that buyers filter by. Magento's product and attribute model was designed for that scale, provided the indexing, search and hosting are set up by people who know the platform.

We are candid about fit. Magento costs more to run than Shopify or WooCommerce and needs regular patching. For a straightforward consumer store we will usually recommend something simpler, and we build on those platforms as well.

sections.heading: Services we provide on Magento
paragraphs: Work is done on a staging environment that mirrors production, to platform standards, with no changes to core code. That keeps the store upgradeable.
bullets: Custom modules for pricing logic, checkout steps, product types and admin tools.
B2B builds: company accounts, tiered and customer-specific price lists, quote requests and purchase approval.
Two-way sync of products, stock, orders and customers with ERP, CRM, POS and fulfilment systems.
Performance work: full-page caching, database and indexer tuning, frontend and image optimisation.
Version upgrades from end-of-life releases, security patching and hardening.
Multi-store setups for several brands or regions managed from one installation.

sections.heading: Integration is where projects succeed or fail
paragraphs: A distributor's website is only as good as the data behind it. If stock on the site disagrees with stock in the warehouse, buyers stop trusting it and go back to phoning their rep. We map each data flow before building: which system owns prices, how often inventory updates, what happens to an order when a line is back-ordered. The integration is then tested with real order scenarios, including the awkward ones.

Tax needs similar care for Texas sellers. Many trade customers buy for resale and are exempt when a valid certificate is on file, while others are taxable at a rate that varies by delivery address. The store should record exemption status per account and apply it without manual edits. Your tax adviser sets the rules and we implement them.

sections.heading: Taking over an existing store
paragraphs: Plenty of Magento stores in Dallas were built years ago by a team that has since moved on. We begin with a code and performance audit, list what is unsafe, what is slow and what blocks an upgrade, and give you a prioritised plan. If the audit shows the business has outgrown or undergrown Magento, we say so and outline a re-platform.

presence: TDM supports Dallas merchants on Magento remotely. We have no office and no staff in Dallas. Development, integration testing and releases are managed online through staging environments you can access.

faqs.q: Is Magento worth it for a Dallas distributor?
faqs.a: Often, yes. If you need customer-specific pricing, company accounts, a very large catalogue or tight ERP integration, Magento handles those natively. If your needs are simpler, a lighter platform will cost less to own, and we will tell you which side of that line you are on.

faqs.q: Can Magento connect to our ERP system?
faqs.a: In most cases. We integrate through the ERP's API or an established connector and define which system is the source of truth for prices, stock and customers. The exact approach depends on your ERP and its version, which we review during discovery.

faqs.q: Our Magento store is on an old version. Can you upgrade it?
faqs.a: Yes. We audit the custom code and extensions, replace anything that will not survive the upgrade, and carry out the move on staging first. Running an unsupported version leaves known security holes open, so this is worth scheduling early.

faqs.q: How much does Magento development cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the scope: catalogue complexity, the number of integrations and how much custom logic is involved. We prepare a quote after a free consultation and, for existing stores, an audit.

faqs.q: What is the timeline for a Magento project?
faqs.a: That is set by your requirements and the brief, especially the integrations. We agree phases and dates in the plan once discovery is complete.
